Hi Alice and Bob,

Thanks again for the call earlier — really appreciate the frank discussion on the observability and performance needs for your generative search POC. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align the POC scope: 

1) Recap from our call:
- Goal: validate inference economics and observability for Acme search at 1k qps sustained bursts to 5k for peak windows.
- Key success metrics: p95 latency under 250ms, tail latency under 500ms, per-token cost below your threshold, and detailed per-route telemetry for SLA reporting.
- Concerns: how vendor consoles surface per-token breakdowns, tracing across request chains, and ability to run comparative tests vs your current hyperscaler endpoint.

2) Proposed next steps (can start week of Mar 9):
- Redwood will provision a sandbox tenant with a dedicated small pool for the POC. Monica will propose exact instance sizes and runbook.
- Run comparative tests: baseline vs hyperscaler with the same model family and prompt sets. Tests include latency percentiles, throughput, token cost, cold vs warm cache, and tail behavior under concurrent KV cache workloads.
- Observability check: share a demo dashboard (attached link) showing per-route token breakdown, top tokens, and trace links to correlate latency spikes to batching and kernel selection.

Attachments: redwood-observability-onepager.pdf (one-page feature summary), acme_poc-map.xlsx (proposed mutual action plan). Demo link: https://redwood.app/console/demo/acme-dashboard

Would you be available for a 30 minute sync next Wednesday to lock down the test matrix? If so, I can send a calendar invite and Monica can share the technical runbook.

Alice — great questions. I put together the high-level checklist below and attached a draft MAP (acme_poc-map.xlsx). Monica, feel free to adjust the runbook details.

High-level test checklist (we recommend running each test for a 30 minute window, multiple runs):
- Baseline throughput: ramp to 1k qps steady state, measure p50/p90/p95/p99 and error rate.
- Peak burst: short 5 minute bursts to 5k qps to measure queuing and tail latency.
- Cold vs warm KV cache: measure first-request vs warmed-cache latencies and token counts.
- Cost per token breakdown: run a representative prompt set and capture per-route token totals, batching efficiency, and estimated USD/unit.
- Trace correlation: capture a sample of traces for any outlier requests to see batching behavior and kernel selection path.
- Integration/observability validation: verify per-route dashboards, alerting hooks, and ability to export logs to your existing SIEM.

Competitive notes you can share with infra:
- Hyperscalers: typically provide endpoint metrics but lack per-token cost breakdowns and fine-grained per-route dashboards. They also often route requests through multi-tenant nodes making tail behavior harder to diagnose.
- Redwood: per-route and per-token dashboards, tracing hooks to link tokens to traces, prefix/KV cache visibility, and automated recommendations for batching and quantization to optimize cost without degrading quality.

Proposed calendar: March 11 at 10am PT for a 30 minute kickoff. Monica will send the technical runbook and resource request.

Thanks,
Marissa

Internal note and tech plan draft — leaving here so the thread is complete.

Marissa/Rishi/Laura,

Proposed technical test plan (more detail):
- Environment: provision a sandbox tenant with 2 x A100-equivalent GPU nodes for dedicated pool. Configure the model to match Acme's current family and use a 4096 token context.
- Load patterns: use vegeta-like runner with the following phases:
  * Warmup: 5 minutes at 200 qps
  * Steady: 30 minutes at 1k qps
  * Burst: 5 x 1 minute bursts to 5k qps with 30s between bursts
- Metrics to capture: p50/90/95/99, tail latency histograms, CPU/GPU utilization, batching stats (avg batch size, batch latency), KV cache hit rates, per-token cost estimate, and sampled traces with full span details.
- Commands (example):
  * loadtest --targets prompts.json --rate 1000 --duration 1800 --concurrency 200
  * redwoodctl metrics export --tenant acme-poc --start 2026-03-11T17:00Z --end 2026-03-11T17:30Z
- Observability checks: enable per-route dashboards, add an alert on p95 > 350ms, and configure trace export to your Datadog project.

Questions for ops: do we have capacity to spin up the dedicated pool for March 11, or should we run on a provisioned shared sandbox with affinity? If dedicated required, I need Laura's approval for a short-term capacity allocation.

I'll prepare the runbook and a one-click dashboard link to hand over during the kickoff.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
